name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q01 - Male testis dimensions and external genitalia

questiontext.text:
Read the following four statements regarding the human male reproductive system:

Statement I: In adults, each testis is oval in shape, measuring about \(4\text{--}5\text{ cm}\) in length and \(2\text{--}3\text{ cm}\) in width, and contains about \(250\) testicular lobules.

Statement II: Each testicular lobule contains one to three highly coiled seminiferous tubules in which sperms are produced.

Statement III: The enlarged end of the penis called the glans penis is covered by a loose fold of skin called the foreskin.

Statement IV: Secretions of the prostate gland alone help in the lubrication of the penis.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The male reproductive system comprises the testes (organised into lobules and seminiferous tubules), accessory ducts, accessory glands, and the penis as external genitalia.

Step 2: Evaluation of Testicular Anatomy
An adult human testis is oval, about \(4\text{--}5\text{ cm}\) long and \(2\text{--}3\text{ cm}\) wide, covered by a dense covering, and partitioned into roughly \(250\) compartments called testicular lobules. Each lobule houses one to three highly coiled seminiferous tubules where sperm production occurs.

Step 3: Evaluation of External Genitalia and Glandular Lubrication
The penis is made of special erectile tissue facilitating insemination, and its enlarged distal end, the glans penis, is covered by a loose fold of skin called the foreskin. However, lubrication of the penis is aided by the secretions of the paired bulbourethral glands, not the prostate gland alone.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The three claims describing adult testicular dimensions and lobule counts, the presence of one to three seminiferous tubules per lobule, and the foreskin covering the glans penis are correct, whereas attributing penile lubrication exclusively to the prostate gland is incorrect.

answer.text: All statements I, II, III and IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q02 - Ovarian stroma fallopian tube and uterus

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements about the human female reproductive system:

Statement I: Each ovary is about \(2\text{--}4\text{ cm}\) in length and its stroma is divided into a peripheral cortex and an inner medulla.

Statement II: Each fallopian tube is about \(10\text{--}12\text{ cm}\) long, and its last part, the isthmus, has a narrow lumen that joins the uterus.

Statement III: The uterus is single, shaped like an inverted pear, and is supported by ligaments attached to the pelvic wall.

Statement IV: The ampulla is the funnel-shaped part of the oviduct closest to the ovary, bearing finger-like projections called fimbriae.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The female reproductive system integrates the ovaries, oviducts (fallopian tubes), uterus, cervix, vagina, and external genitalia to support ovulation, fertilisation, pregnancy, and birth.

Step 2: Evaluation of Ovarian and Uterine Structure
Each ovary measures about \(2\text{--}4\text{ cm}\) in length, is tethered to the pelvic wall and uterus by ligaments, and contains stroma divided into a peripheral cortex and an inner medulla. The single uterus (womb) has an inverted-pear shape and is similarly supported by ligaments attached to the pelvic wall.

Step 3: Evaluation of Fallopian Tube Regions
Each fallopian tube is \(10\text{--}12\text{ cm}\) long, extending from the ovary's periphery to the uterus. Its terminal region, the isthmus, has a narrow lumen and joins the uterus. However, the funnel-shaped region closest to the ovary bearing fimbriae is the infundibulum, which leads into the wider ampulla—not the ampulla itself.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims describing ovarian dimensions and stromal zonation, fallopian tube length with the narrow-lumened isthmus, and the inverted-pear shape of the uterus are correct, whereas identifying the ampulla as the funnel-shaped part with fimbriae is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q03 - Mammary gland lobes and spermatid ploidy

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements regarding human mammary glands and spermatogenesis:

Statement I: The glandular tissue of each breast is divided into \(15\text{--}20\) mammary lobes containing clusters of milk-secreting cells called alveoli.

Statement II: Spermatogenesis in males begins at puberty due to a significant increase in the secretion of hypothalamic \(\text{GnRH}\).

Statement III: Secondary spermatocytes undergo the second meiotic division to produce four equal haploid spermatids, each containing \(23\) chromosomes.

Statement IV: Sperm heads become embedded in Leydig cells after spermiogenesis before being released by spermiation.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Functional mammary glands are characteristic of female mammals for child care, while spermatogenesis in males begins at puberty under hypothalamic-pituitary control.

Step 2: Evaluation of Mammary Gland and Spermatogenesis Claims
Each breast contains glandular tissue divided into \(15\text{--}20\) mammary lobes housing clusters of alveoli whose cells secrete milk into alveolar lumens. In males, spermatogenesis initiates at puberty following a marked rise in hypothalamic \(\text{GnRH}\), and meiosis II of secondary spermatocytes yields four equal haploid spermatids, each with \(23\) chromosomes.

Step 3: Evaluation of Spermiation Attachment
After spermatids differentiate into spermatozoa (spermiogenesis), the sperm heads become embedded in Sertoli cells inside the seminiferous tubules—not in Leydig cells, which lie outside in the interstitial spaces—before release via spermiation.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding the \(15\text{--}20\) mammary lobes with alveoli, puberty-onset \(\text{GnRH}\)-driven spermatogenesis, and \(23\)-chromosome haploid spermatids are correct, while the claim that sperm heads embed in Leydig cells is incorrect.

answer.text: All statements I, II, III and IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q04 - Follicular stages and Graafian follicle ovulation

questiontext.text:
Examine the following four statements regarding ovarian follicular development during oogenesis:

Statement I: Oogonia in the fetal ovary enter prophase-I of meiosis and get temporarily arrested at that stage as primary oocytes.

Statement II: A primary oocyte surrounded by a layer of granulosa cells is called a primary follicle, which later acquires more granulosa layers and a new theca to form a secondary follicle.

Statement III: The tertiary follicle is characterised by a fluid-filled cavity called the antrum and a theca organised into an inner theca interna and an outer theca externa.

Statement IV: The zona pellucida is formed around the primary oocyte prior to birth, and the secondary follicle directly ruptures to release the primary oocyte during ovulation.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Oogenesis in human females involves sequential follicular maturation from primary to secondary, tertiary, and mature Graafian follicles, coupled with meiotic progression.

Step 2: Evaluation of Early and Tertiary Follicular Stages
Fetal oogonia enter prophase-I and arrest as primary oocytes; each surrounded by a granulosa layer forms a primary follicle. Addition of more granulosa layers and a new theca creates a secondary follicle, which transforms into a tertiary follicle featuring a fluid-filled antrum and a two-layered theca (theca interna and theca externa).

Step 3: Evaluation of Zona Pellucida and Ovulation
Inside the tertiary follicle, the primary oocyte completes meiosis I to form a secondary oocyte. As the tertiary follicle matures into the Graafian follicle, the secondary oocyte forms a new membrane called the zona pellucida around it, and it is the Graafian follicle (not the secondary follicle) that ruptures to release the secondary oocyte during ovulation.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims describing prophase-I arrest, primary-to-secondary follicle transition, and the tertiary follicle with antrum and bilaminar theca are correct, whereas the claim regarding prenatal zona pellucida formation and secondary follicle rupture is incorrect.

answer.text: All statements I, II, III and IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q05 - Menstrual cycle phases and hormonal dynamics

questiontext.text:
Analyse the following four statements regarding the events and hormonal control of the human menstrual cycle:

Statement I: During the follicular phase, primary follicles grow into a mature Graafian follicle while the uterine endometrium regenerates through proliferation.

Statement II: Both \(\text{LH}\) and \(\text{FSH}\) attain a peak level in the middle of the cycle (about the \(14\text{th}\) day), inducing ovulation.

Statement III: During the luteal phase, the corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone, which is essential for maintaining the endometrium for implantation.

Statement IV: During pregnancy, follicular maturation continues normally, though menstrual bleeding is temporarily suppressed by high \(\text{FSH}\) levels.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The menstrual cycle coordinates ovarian follicular maturation and ovulation with cyclic endometrial preparation for potential implantation, governed by pituitary gonadotropins and ovarian steroids.

Step 2: Evaluation of Follicular, Ovulatory, and Luteal Phases
In the follicular (proliferative) phase, rising gonadotropins drive growth of primary follicles into a Graafian follicle and estrogen-mediated endometrial proliferation. Around day \(14\), \(\text{LH}\) and \(\text{FSH}\) peak and the \(\text{LH}\) surge induces ovulation. Thereafter, in the luteal phase, the corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone to maintain the endometrium for implantation.

Step 3: Evaluation of Pregnancy Status
During pregnancy, all events of the menstrual cycle stop completely—there is no menstruation and no cyclic follicular maturation—maintained by high levels of pregnancy hormones rather than \(\text{FSH}\)-mediated suppression alone.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The three claims covering follicular-phase endometrial regeneration, the mid-cycle \(\text{LH}\) and \(\text{FSH}\) peak causing ovulation, and luteal progesterone maintenance of the endometrium are correct, whereas the claim that follicular maturation continues normally during pregnancy is incorrect.

answer.text: All statements I, II, III and IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q06 - Fertilisation acrosome action and blastocyst implantation

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding fertilisation and early embryonic development:

Statement I: During coitus, semen is released into the vagina (insemination), and motile sperms pass through the cervix and uterus to reach the ampullary region of the fallopian tube.

Statement II: Acrosomal secretions help the sperm enter the cytoplasm of the ovum through the zona pellucida and plasma membrane.

Statement III: Fusion of the haploid sperm nucleus and the haploid ovum nucleus forms a diploid zygote.

Statement IV: After attachment of the blastocyst, uterine cells divide rapidly and cover the blastocyst so that it becomes embedded in the myometrium.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Fertilisation requires sperm transport through the female genital tract to the ampullary region, enzymatic penetration of ovum coverings, nuclear fusion, and subsequent uterine implantation of the blastocyst.

Step 2: Evaluation of Sperm Transport, Entry, and Zygote Formation
Semen deposited in the vagina during coitus releases motile sperms that swim through the cervix and uterus to the ampullary region. Acrosomal enzymes facilitate entry through the zona pellucida and plasma membrane, triggering meiosis II completion and fusion of the two haploid nuclei into a diploid zygote.

Step 3: Evaluation of Implantation Layer
Following cleavage into a morula and blastocyst, the trophoblast attaches to the inner glandular lining of the uterus—the endometrium—and rapidly dividing uterine cells cover the blastocyst so it embeds in the endometrium, not the muscular myometrium.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims describing sperm transport to the ampulla, acrosomal assistance in sperm entry, and diploid zygote formation are correct, while stating that the blastocyst embeds in the myometrium instead of the endometrium is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q07 - Placenta umbilical cord and maternal pregnancy hormones

questiontext.text:
Read the following four statements regarding pregnancy and embryonic support systems:

Statement I: The placenta is connected to the developing embryo through an umbilical cord that helps transport substances to and from the embryo.

Statement II: The placenta acts as an endocrine tissue producing hormones such as \(\text{hCG}\), \(\text{hPL}\), estrogens, and progestogens.

Statement III: During pregnancy, maternal blood levels of cortisol, prolactin, thyroxine, estrogens, and progestogens increase several-fold to support foetal growth and maternal metabolic changes.

Statement IV: After implantation, the inner cell mass differentiates into ectoderm and endoderm only, while mesoderm arises from the trophoblast.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
During pregnancy, the placenta and umbilical cord sustain foetal exchange and endocrine signalling, while the inner cell mass establishes the three primary germ layers.

Step 2: Evaluation of Placental Connection and Hormonal Changes
The umbilical cord links the placenta to the embryo for bidirectional transport of gases, nutrients, and wastes. As an endocrine organ, the placenta secretes \(\text{hCG}\), \(\text{hPL}\), estrogens, and progestogens; concurrently, maternal blood concentrations of estrogens, progestogens, cortisol, prolactin, and thyroxine rise several-fold to support foetal growth, maternal metabolism, and pregnancy maintenance.

Step 3: Evaluation of Germ Layer Origin
Immediately after implantation, the inner cell mass differentiates into an outer ectoderm and an inner endoderm, and the mesoderm soon appears between them—meaning all three germ layers derive from the inner cell mass, not from the trophoblast.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims describing the umbilical cord transport link, placental hormone secretion, and multi-fold maternal hormone elevation are accurate, whereas attributing mesoderm origin to the trophoblast is incorrect.

answer.text: All statements I, II, III and IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q08 - Fetal development milestones and parturition expulsion

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements regarding human embryonic milestones and parturition:

Statement I: By the end of \(12\) weeks (first trimester), most major organ systems, including limbs and external genital organs, are well-developed.

Statement II: By the end of about \(24\) weeks (end of second trimester), the foetal body is covered with fine hair, eyelids separate, and eyelashes are formed.

Statement III: Parturition is induced by a complex neuroendocrine mechanism involving cortisol, estrogens, and oxytocin, and soon after infant delivery the placenta is also expelled from the uterus.

Statement IV: The foetal ejection reflex is initiated solely by the maternal pituitary gland without any signals from the foetus or placenta.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Human gestation spans approximately \(9\) months of progressive organogenesis and growth, culminating in parturition driven by a coordinated neuroendocrine reflex.

Step 2: Evaluation of First and Second Trimester Milestones
By the end of \(12\) weeks (first trimester), most major organ systems—such as limbs and external genital organs—are well-formed. By the end of about \(24\) weeks (second trimester), fine hair covers the body, eyelids separate, and eyelashes develop.

Step 3: Evaluation of Parturition Signals and Expulsion
Parturition is mediated by a complex neuroendocrine mechanism involving cortisol, estrogens, and oxytocin, and the placenta is expelled from the uterus shortly after delivery of the baby. However, the signals initiating the mild uterine contractions of the foetal ejection reflex originate from the fully developed foetus and the placenta, which then trigger oxytocin release from the maternal pituitary—not from the maternal pituitary alone.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The three claims regarding the \(12\)-week and \(24\)-week foetal milestones and the neuroendocrine induction of parturition with subsequent placental expulsion are correct, whereas claiming that the foetal ejection reflex starts solely in the maternal pituitary without foetal or placental signals is incorrect.

answer.text: All statements I, II, III and IV
